Incoterms 2020

Orden de entrega

A document issued by carrier or agent instructing terminal or warehouse to release cargo to the consignee or their agent.

Why it matters

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Orden de entrega?

In this glossary, Orden de entrega refers to: A document issued by carrier or agent instructing terminal or warehouse to release cargo to the consignee or their agent.

How is Orden de entrega used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "El transitario presentó la orden de entrega en la terminal de contenedores para liberar la mercancía importada."

Why does Orden de entrega matter in logistics?

Orden de entrega matters because it supports clear communication in Incoterms 2020 contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Who uses Orden de entrega?

Orden de entrega is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

What category does Orden de entrega belong to?

In this glossary, Orden de entrega is grouped under Incoterms 2020. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A document issued by carrier or agent instructing terminal or warehouse to release cargo to the consignee or their agent.

Operational example

The freight forwarder presented the delivery order at the container terminal to obtain release of the imported goods.

Localized term
